requestedActions.title: List issue titles in projects the connected person can access, with pagination

guide.summary: GitLab documents OAuth 2 authorization code with PKCE and the read_api scope, which grants read access to the API including projects. Its documented project issues list endpoint supports the read-only issue-title request with pagination. Registration, the connected person's project role, and token expiry remain setup or test prerequisites.
guide.recommendation: The requested API test is not ready yet. Resolve the access mapping for List issue titles in projects the connected person can access, with pagination. Use “Find missing request” or add official documentation beside that action.

findings.title: GitLab documents OAuth 2 authorization code with PKCE for user-level API access
findings.detail: The OAuth 2 identity provider API documents the authorization code with PKCE flow for user-authorized access, and the token is used to make API requests on behalf of a user.
findings.appliesWhen: The customer connects an individual account and the app calls the REST API as that user.

evidence.quote: Authorization code with Proof Key for Code Exchange (PKCE) :
Authorization code (with or without PKCE) flow requires application to be
The access token allows you to make requests to the API on behalf of a user.

findings.title: read_api grants read access to the API including all groups and projects
findings.detail: read_api is the narrowest documented API scope that covers reading project issues; the api scope adds read/write access, so it is not needed. The scope boundary includes projects the user can access, but the user's own project role still governs what they can see.
findings.appliesWhen: Use for the read-only issue title request on the REST API.

evidence.quote: read_api Grants read access to the API, including all groups and projects, the container registry, and the package registry.

findings.title: Register a user-owned OAuth application with a redirect URI before testing
findings.detail: A user-owned application requires a name, redirect URI and OAuth scopes; GitLab then provides the client ID and client secret used in the authorization flow.

findings.title: Connected person must already have a project role that can view issues
findings.detail: Users with only the Minimal Access role cannot view project features such as issues. Guest and higher roles can view issues on private and internal projects, so the connected person must be confirmed to have access to each project.
findings.appliesWhen: The connected person's account must have access to the projects whose issue titles are listed.

evidence.quote: Users with only this role cannot view project features such as wikis, issues, or the repository. To
Guest View and comment on issues and epics. Cannot push code or access repository. This role applies to private and internal projects only.
The Minimal Access role grants none of the permissions in the group and project permission tables.

findings.title: Access tokens expire after two hours and need refresh-token handling
findings.detail: By default OAuth access tokens expire after 7200 seconds. Integrations must use the refresh_token to obtain a new access token; the refresh token remains usable after the access token expires.
findings.appliesWhen: Pagination across many requests may outlast one access token.

evidence.quote: By default, access tokens expire after two hours (7200 seconds). Integrations that use access tokens must generate a new token with the refresh_token attribute. Refresh tokens can be used even
after the access token itself expires. For information on how to refresh expired access tokens, see OAuth 2.0 token documentation .

steps.title: Register a user-owned OAuth application in GitLab
steps.detail: Create a user-owned application with a Name, a Redirect URI and the read_api scope, then save it. GitLab shows the Application ID (client ID) and Secret. Store the secret securely; it is only shown once unless renewed.
steps.doneWhen: The application appears under Access > Applications with an Application ID and Secret recorded. No consent or token exchange has been performed.

evidence.quote: Create a user-owned application
Enter a Name and Redirect URI .
The OAuth 2 Client ID in the Application ID field.

fields: GITLAB_BASE_URL: customer GitLab origin (use https://gitlab.com for GitLab.com)
REDIRECT_URI: callback URL configured in the application
CLIENT_ID: Application ID shown by GitLab
CLIENT_SECRET: Secret shown by GitLab; keep it confidential

steps.title: Send the connected person through the GitLab authorization URL
steps.detail: Open the authorization URL in a browser, sign in as the individual customer and approve read_api. Confirm the callback receives a code and the returned state matches the value you generated.
steps.doneWhen: The browser is redirected to REDIRECT_URI with code and the same state value. The authorization code is recorded for the next step.

evidence.quote: https://gitlab.example.com/oauth/authorize?client_id=APP_ID&redirect_uri=REDIRECT_URI&response_type=code&state=STATE&scope=REQUESTED_SCOPES&code_challenge=CODE_CHALLENGE&code_challenge_method=S256&root_namespace_id=ROOT_NAMESPACE_ID This page asks
The redirect includes the authorization code , for example:

fields: APP_ID: Application ID from registration
REDIRECT_URI: must match the registered redirect URI
STATE: random value you generate and verify on callback
CODE_CHALLENGE: S256 hash of CODE_VERIFIER (PKCE)
INSTANCE_BASE_URL: your full HTTPS instance URL, without a trailing slash

steps.title: Exchange the authorization code for an access token
steps.detail: POST the returned code and the PKCE CODE_VERIFIER to the token endpoint. The response includes access_token, refresh_token and expires_in.
steps.doneWhen: The token response contains access_token, refresh_token and expires_in. Do not log token values.

evidence.quote: ruby parameters = 'client_id=APP_ID&code=RETURNED_CODE&grant_type=authorization_code&redirect_uri=REDIRECT_URI&code_verifier=CODE_VERIFIER'
Example response: json {

fields: RETURNED_CODE: code from the callback in the previous step
CODE_VERIFIER: the random verifier used to build CODE_CHALLENGE
grant_type: authorization_code (documented constant)
INSTANCE_BASE_URL: your full HTTPS instance URL, without a trailing slash

steps.title: List issue titles in a project with the connected person's token
steps.detail: Call the documented project issues list endpoint with the access token. Read title from each object in the returned array. Use a representative project ID the developer provides; do not enumerate projects.
steps.doneWhen: The response is a JSON array of issue objects and each object's title field is present. Output lists titles only. Boundary check: inspect the actual grant against the documented access above; confirm the outgoing request log contains only the requested operations and no prohibited actions.

fields: PROJECT_ID: representative project ID provided by the developer
OAUTH-TOKEN: access_token from the exchange step
$[].title: JSON path to each issue title string

steps.detail: Use a documented read-only check: inspect the grant and the outgoing request log to confirm only GET requests were made. Do not send any write request to test this.
steps.doneWhen: Grant shows read_api only and the request log contains only GET calls to issue endpoints.

steps.title: Request the next page of project issues
steps.detail: Repeat the list request with page=2 (offset pagination, same per_page and filters). Continue while the page returns a non-empty array; stop when an empty array is returned. Keyset pagination is available via pagination=keyset for consecutive pages.
steps.doneWhen: Page 2 returns issue objects with title fields, or an empty array marks the end of the collection. Boundary check: inspect the actual grant against the documented access above; confirm the outgoing request log contains only the requested operations and no prohibited actions.

blockers.title: List issue titles in projects the connected person can access, with pagination
blockers.resolution: Offset pagination's empty-array end condition is documented only for keyset pagination, so replace the page-number stop rule with following the documented Link header rel="next" URL from each response until it is absent, or use keyset pagination only if the issues endpoint's keyset support is documented. Affected steps: pagination-continuation, pagination-continuation-2.
